physics_gate_2.check_values_in_tests: tests/test_physics.gd asserts package values for illuminanceFromV(0), (-1.46), pointFluxRatio(60 kK, 44.7), (60 kK, 1/44.7), (3300 K, sqrt 19), Y(1e7)/Y(1e6); I recomputed every one with sunholo/relativity 0.5.1 through ailang (scratch package) and with an independent pure-Python oracle (Planck x Wyman CMF): all agree to <= 2e-16 relative. Spec RS-1..RS-4, RS-Q1, RS-Q2 remain asserted by the existing tests.
physics_gate_2.doppler_convention: shader (sky/starfield.gdshader:48-57) and CPU (physics/relativity.gd doppler) both use D = gamma (1 + beta cos theta) with theta the galaxy-frame angle of the same n that is aberrated, which equals 1/(gamma (1 - beta cos theta')) of the spec; sideways (apparent 90 deg) gives 1/gamma, blueshift only inside cos theta' > (1 - 1/gamma)/beta (51.2 deg at 0.9c, 29.8 deg at 0.99c), matching the renders. 1 + beta cos theta is rewritten as (1 - beta) + beta (1 + cos theta) for cos theta < 0 with 1 - beta formed in float64 on the CPU.
physics_gate_2.brightness_law: splat energy = E_v |p|^2 / r^2 x pointFluxRatio(T, D) = Y(D T)/Y(T)/D^2 (spec point-source law; bolometric D^2, not D^4). Golden hot WD: GPU integrated luminance / unit star = 1.0022 under a linear tonemapper.
physics_gate_2.gpu_golden: make golden AILANG=$A: 0 failures (144 off-axis + 16 background markers + 4 stand-off + hot WD + cull + 9 original cases)
physics_gate_2.maths_mirrored_from_package: Relativity.illuminance_from_v and point_flux_ratio mirror photometry.illuminanceFromV and blackbody.pointFluxRatio of sunholo/relativity 0.5.1 (sim/ailang.toml pins 0.5.1); the shader mirrors the GDScript.
physics_gate_2.float64_precision: positions PackedFloat64Array; ship position passed as three float64 scalars (never through a Vector3); hi/lo float32 split on upload; gamma and 1 - beta from float64 on the CPU.
physics_gate_2.lut_finite: existing test loops every texel for finiteness and monotonicity over the new 300 K..1e7 K range (1320 texels); the shader clamps u to [0, 1] so D T outside the range (e.g. 3000 K at D 0.071 -> 213 K) reads the end texel, finite.

renders_opened.my_capture: make capture AILANG=$A AILANG_BIN=$A on the large tier: starfield: tiers [large], 324307 stars drawn, 7005 without photometry skipped, rebase GPU; 20 PNGs + contact sheet, all opened
renders_opened.b00_forward: natural sky: Milky Way band, orange/white stars, few bright ones (GCNS lacks the naked-eye bright stars until the M1.2d bright tier). Physically right for GCNS at rest.
renders_opened.b05_forward: mild crowding, the plane brightened (D ahead 1.73), stars slightly bluer. Right.
renders_opened.b09_forward: stars crowd into the forward hemisphere and are blue-white; the field is dense out to ~50 deg (blueshift cone 51.2 deg) because beamed M dwarfs (pointFluxRatio(3300 K, sqrt 19) = 26.3) rise above the cull. The plane is compressed and bright. Right.
renders_opened.b09_starboard: dim: only the left edge (apparent angles < ~52 deg from the heading) shows stars; the rest is dark with a faint reddish band; one orange star at apparent 52 deg has D 0.976 (slight redshift). Sideways D = 1/gamma = 0.43 (5700 K -> 2480 K). Right.
renders_opened.b09_astern: black. D = 0.229: a V = 0 G star becomes V ~12.7 in the visual band (pointFluxRatio 7.9e-6), below the cull; the background likewise. Right per the band law.
renders_opened.b099_forward: a tight cone of ~30 deg radius (blueshift cone 29.8 deg), blue-white stars, the galactic plane compressed into a thin bright line. Right.
renders_opened.b099_offaxis: view 54.4 deg from v: stars only at the right edge, inside the cone. Right.
renders_opened.b099_rolled: the cone in the upper left, the plane as a rolled streak. Right.

spot_checks.method: pure-Python oracle (scratch, untracked): reads stars_large.bin, applies galactic->world, inverse-square, aberration, D, pointFluxRatio and the FreeLookCamera pinhole projection (fov 70, 960x540) from the ship positions the sim printed at capture, then measures the luminance centroid within +-4 px of each predicted pixel on my own renders
spot_checks.positions: 32 brightest predicted stars across b00_forward, b09_forward, b099_forward, b09_starboard: 30 within 0.1-0.8 px of the rendered centroid; 2 at 1.2 and 2.2 px where a neighbour or the frame edge biases the window. Example: GCNS row 250475 (3870 K, V 2.81, 131-137 ly) at theta 10.3 deg rest -> 2.38 deg apparent at 0.9c (D 4.34) -> 0.76 deg at 0.99c (D 14.0); rendered at (455.8, 335.6), (474.0, 284.7), (478.0, 274.7) vs predicted (456.0, 335.9), (474.5, 285.1), (478.2, 274.8).
spot_checks.brightness: rendered local sums track the predicted post-beaming flux ordering: the same star rises from peak 0.377 (168,144,117: orange) at rest to 4.49 (239,243,249: blue-white) at 0.9c; predicted peaks 0.3-0.5 render at 140-177/255 under AgX, peaks 2.6-4.5 at 234-255. Quantitative brightness is covered by the hot-WD golden under a linear tonemapper (1.0022).

v_extent = sqrt(2 ln(peak / cull_peak)) cuts the quad where the PSF equals cull_peak, so a star of peak p loses cull_peak / p of its integrated energy (10% at p = 1e-3, about V 9.2 at rest; 1% at 1e-2). Invisible under AgX, but 'splat energy proportional to E_v' holds only well above the cull.
non_blocking.suggestion: Document the bound, or add +1 sigma to the extent (cost: a slightly larger quad for faint stars).
